solution.key_idea: Jade's and Vito's statements are opposites about Otis, so they use up the one true statement, and Otis's must be false.
steps: With three suspects, Jade's "Vito or I" means Otis didn't sound the horn, and Vito's "neither Jade nor I" means Otis did.
So Jade and Vito say opposite things, and exactly one of them is telling the truth.
The rule allows exactly one true statement, and that pair uses it up. So Otis's statement is false.
Otis says Vito or Otis sounded the horn. That is false, so neither did, and Jade sounded the horn.
Check Jade: only Jade's own statement is true, so Jade fits. Testing Otis or Vito gives two true statements each.
solution.epilogue: Jade, the ferry's relief deckhand, had come aboard for her forgotten thermos and leaned on the horn button in the dark. She apologized to Jonah, and to Pilot, before the 7:30 sailing.
